migration.title: 10 Myths About Migration & Refugees
migration.summary: An accessible, referenced teaching booklet by Tony Daly and Ciara Regan. Use its questions to examine migration claims and discuss the people behind the statistics.
migration.limitation: Background reading: its statistics and asylum rules are historical. Use current sources below to check today’s figures and procedures.

migration.title: Information Hub
migration.summary: Refugee-rights guidance that helps separate the international protection process from rumours. The hub provides different information for applications made before, or on or after, 12 June 2026.
migration.limitation: Choose the route that matches the application date. Follow the publisher’s updates; general information does not resolve an individual legal case.

migration.title: Monitoring Report on Integration 2024
migration.summary: National survey and administrative evidence on employment, education, social inclusion and citizenship. A strong starting point for checking broad claims about migrants’ lives in Ireland.
migration.limitation: Read each indicator’s reference year. “Foreign-born”, “non-Irish citizen” and “person seeking asylum” describe different groups.

migration.title: Learn About Racism in Ireland
migration.summary: Definitions, learning materials and research from Ireland’s anti-racism network. Helps identify stereotyping and understand how discrimination can operate through institutions as well as individual behaviour.
migration.limitation: Anti-racist education and a route to evidence; this is not a population count or a migration statistics release.

migration.title: EMN Asylum and Migration Glossary
migration.summary: A multilingual reference for migration and asylum terminology. Check what a term means before comparing figures or repeating a claim that mixes different migration categories.
migration.limitation: Definitions have a stated EU or international context. They do not determine a particular person’s immigration status.

migration.publisher: Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development
migration.title: International Migration Outlook 2025
migration.summary: Comparative evidence on migration, work and integration, with country notes and a statistical annex. Useful for testing sweeping international comparisons and claims about migrant workers.
migration.limitation: Use the country, migration category and data year attached to each table. An OECD average is not an Irish or local figure.

migration.date_scope_type: Updated February 2026 · United Kingdom · Evidence briefing
migration.title: The Labour Market Effects of Immigration
migration.purpose: Look closely at jobs and wages
migration.summary: Explains research on employment and wages, including why effects differ between groups and why measuring cause and effect is difficult. Links to the studies behind the analysis.
migration.limitation: UK evidence: useful for understanding the question, but it cannot establish the size of an effect in Saggart, Citywest or Ireland.

migration.title: Being Black in the EU
migration.summary: Survey evidence on racism experienced by people of African descent, including respondents in Ireland. The report provides its questionnaire and technical information for readers to examine.
migration.limitation: The surveyed population is specific. These findings do not describe every migrant, every minority ethnic group or this local community.

migration.title: Antirumours Handbook
migration.summary: A structured method for identifying rumours, gathering evidence and involving residents in challenging prejudice. Particularly useful for community groups planning sustained anti-racism work.
migration.limitation: A practical methodology with historical examples, rather than a source of current migration totals.

migration.title: Claiming the Power of Dialogue
migration.summary: A shorter toolkit for responding to stereotypes and misinformation in conversation. Covers listening, building a connection, correcting a claim and reflecting on what helped.
migration.limitation: Use alongside sound evidence and respect for people’s dignity. A conversation toolkit cannot verify a factual claim on its own.
